if I were there

How today would have gone

I'd have woken you up badly and too early. Made the matcha slightly wrong. Watched you fix it without saying anything. Then spent the whole day being the person holding your bag while you looked incredible.

two years in

Things I know for certain

That you laugh before the punchline. That you'll redo an outfit three times and the first one was already perfect. That you say "just one sip" and finish my whole drink. That a room is better when you're in it, and far too quiet when you're not.

whatever you asked for, I hope it finds you by next August

A year where everything fits — the jeans, the plans, the people.
Matcha that's always the right temperature, on the first try.
A wardrobe that behaves on your busiest mornings.
Fewer bad days — and good company on the ones you still get.
The window seat. Every single time.
One adventure that scares you a little.
People who laugh at your jokes as fast as I do.
And me — closer than I was this year.
one last thing

A small letter, on a big day

Yashi — two years ago today something started that I still can't fully explain, and honestly I've stopped trying. Some things you just get to be lucky about.

I'm sorry I'm not there. I wanted cake and candles and your face doing that thing it does when you're pretending not to be excited. Instead you get this: a page with pink everywhere, because pink is yours. Snoopy and Cinnamoroll, because they're yours too. And a matcha you'll have to drink on my behalf.

Happy birthday to the person who makes ordinary days look styled. Happy anniversary to the best two years I've had. And here's to the next one — this time, in the same room.

All my love, always
